email.subject: Unusual payment: your card has been temporarily paused

body.v: We have held a card payment of CHF 389.00 that looked unusual to us. As a precaution, your card stays paused until we hear back from you.
Please open the SwissAlpBank app within 24 hours and let us know whether you made this payment.
We will never ask you for a code, a password or your card number, whether by email, text message or phone.

hotspots.explain: After the @ it reads swissalpbank.example: the bank's own domain, with nothing added.
The deadline is real, but it sends you to the app you already have, not to a link. Urgency on its own does not make a scam.
The bank says in writing that it will never ask you for a code or a password.
There is no link in the message: it points you to the app, a channel you open yourself.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Read the address, not just the name.
who.answer: SwissAlpBank. The address is on swissalpbank.example, and nothing in the message leads to another domain.
choices: A fake adviser who wants to call you

emotion.prompt: Which feeling is this email pressing on?
emotion.answer: A little urgency: a payment is on hold and you have 24 hours. The pressure comes from a real deadline, with no threat at all.
choices: None, it is just an information notice
A little urgency, tied to a real deadline

ask.prompt: What does it actually want you to do?
ask.answer: Open the app and say whether the payment was yours. No code, no link, no password.
choices: Send back the code that reached your phone
Sign in by following a link
Check a payment in the app

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Open the SwissAlpBank app yourself, or call the number on the back of your card.
choices: Reply to the email to confirm the payment
Look in the email for a link to your account

actions.label: Open the SwissAlpBank app yourself and check the payment
actions.consequence: The held payment is there: you confirm it or dispute it.

actions.label: Call the number on the back of your card
actions.consequence: On the phone, the bank confirms that it did hold this payment.

actions.label: Reply with the code if one arrives
actions.consequence: The email said so: the bank never asks for a code. A code goes to nobody, not even your real bank.

attacker_reveal: Nothing for me in this one: a real deadline, the right domain, and the app you already have. Put it next to the "Case 7731" email: same calm, same amount, but only one of them wants the digits from your text messages.
